Nature Communications: Hippocampal mechanisms underlying the resolution of competition in memory and perception
item.description: Memory and perception both require selecting behaviorally relevant information. Here, the authors show that more distinct hippocampal memories are linked to precise anticipatory signals in visual cortex that prioritize perceptual targets over competitors.

item.title: Nature Communications: DNA-PK driven nucleosome unwrapping enables NHEJ in chromatin
item.description: DNA repair proteins work around nucleosomes, which package DNA in cells and limits DNA accessibility for DNA repair factors. Here, by using cryo-EM and biochemical assays, the authors show that DNA-PKcs promotes NHEJ by overcoming histone barriers and moving along nucleosomal DNA.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multimodal radiopathomics model predicts postoperative metachronous liver metastasis in gastric cancer
item.description: Accurate prediction of metachronous liver metastasis (MLM) after curative surgery for locally advanced gastric cancer (LAGC) remains challenging. Here, the authors develop a multimodal model to predict MLM in LAGC patients by integrating clinical, imaging, and pathology data across multi-centre cohorts, also revealing patients who could be more responsive to adjuvant immunotherapy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Unified down-stream analysis of crosslinking mass spectrometry results with pyXLMS
item.description: Crosslinking mass spectrometry (XLMS) has become the method of choice for uncovering protein interactions and structure in vivo. Here, the authors present pyXLMS – a python package and web application – to streamline the down-stream analysis of XLMS results to extract biological meaning.

item.title: Nature Communications: Brain control of hepatic bile acid homeostasis through Bdnf exon I-positive neurons in the paraventricular hypothalamus
item.description: The authors show a brain-liver axis in which PVH Bdnf -e1-expressing neurons regulate hepatic bile acid metabolism. Findings provide new insights into the central regulation of liver metabolism and suggest a potential therapeutic target for MAFLD.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phosphorylation-dependent control of transcription factor activity regulates temporal patterning of cortical cell fate specification
item.description: Here, researchers reveal how chemical tags on two proteins act as a molecular timer during brain development, guiding stem cells to first multiply, then mature into neurons—offering new insight into how the cerebral cortex is built.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global lake tipping vulnerability under sustained agricultural exposure
item.description: Lakes tip into degraded states mainly because of what already surrounds them, not new developments. Chronic agricultural exposure and baseline water quality globally predict abrupt shifts better than early warning signals.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural identification of the RY12 domain of RyR1 as an ADP sensor and the target of the malignant hyperthermia therapeutic dantrolene
item.description: Malignant hyperthermia (MH) is a life-threatening disorder linked to RyR1. Here, Kim et al. use structural and functional data to show the drug dantrolene requires ATP/ADP to bind to the RY12 domain of RyR1, and they identify binding sites of the MH trigger 4-chloro-m-cresol (4CmC).

item.title: Nature Communications: Cost-efficient long-read trio-barcoded adaptive sequencing improves rare disease diagnosis
item.description: Here the authors present Phenotype-driven Trio-barcoded Adaptive Sequencing (TBAS) that enables cost-efficient long-read sequencing of rare-disease trios on a single flow cell, detecting diverse genetic variants while cutting costs to 32% of standard trio sequencing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Higher-order epistasis drives evolutionary unpredictability toward new antibiotic resistance
item.description: Authors investigate the evolution E. coli TEM-1 β-lactamase into ESBLs with a complete library of 55,296 TEM-1 β-lactamase variants, showing that adaptation to a non-native antibiotic is driven by higher-order epistasis, making resistance evolution far less predictable than to the native substrate.

item.title: Nature Communications: CML20 integrates phytochrome and calcium signaling pathways to optimize seed germination under abiotic stress
item.description: Plants integrate multiple environmental cues to time seed germination. Here, the authors show that the calcium-sensing CML20 protein links light and stress signals, enabling seeds to germinate under salt and drought conditions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural and functional insights into QueC-family protein in QatABCD anti-phage system
item.description: Here the authors determine the structure and mechanism of the QatABCD anti-phage defense system, showing how the QueCfamily protein QatC recognizes QatB to enable bacterial antiviral immunity and highlighting a conserved role for QueC-family proteins in protein modification.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fragmentation patterns of human telomeric chromatin in plasma cfDNA
item.description: Telomeres protect the ends of chromosomes, but their structure has been hard to study non-invasively. Here, the authors show that DNA fragments in blood plasma capture this structure, revealing changes with age and in telomere biology disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: Astrocytic PI3Kα controls synaptic plasticity and cognitive function via serine metabolism
item.description: The authors find that the PI3Kα pathway links metabolism to hippocampal synaptic plasticity by sustaining astrocyte glycolysis and ensuring L-serine/D-serine supply to neurons. Loss of astrocytic PI3Kα impairs memory in mice, an effect rescued by serine supplementation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiple local PfDHFR I164L haplotype expansions drive Plasmodium falciparum antifolate resistance in Uganda
item.description: PfDHFR haplotypes involving I164L are known to strongly influence antifolate resistance in Plasmodium falciparum. In this study, Asua and colleagues examine the frequency of antifolate-resistance conferring mutations in over 4,700 parasite samples collected in Uganda over a 6-year period. They report that markers conferring antifolate resistance during this time, which may impact chemotherapeutic strategies that are reliant on sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP).

item.title: Nature Communications: Correlating metabolites, lipids, and N-glycans in murine kidney microstructures via integrative mass spectrometry imaging
item.description: Authors provide a method to map metabolites, lipids and glycans from a single tissue section using mass spectrometry imaging. Applied on murine kidney, the method reveals how molecules across classes correlate in kidney microstructures.

item.title: Nature Communications: Automated kinetic-scheme-free sorting of single-molecule fluorescence events using a deep learning based hidden-state method
item.description: Single-molecule fluorescence reveals hidden biomolecular dynamics, but analysis relies on manual curation and user-defined kinetic models. Here, authors present DASH, an automated framework that sorts events without predefined kinetic schemes, enabling unbiased discovery of molecular complexity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global spectrum of leaf nitrogen allocation driven by evolution and environment
item.description: Plants need nitrogen to absorb CO 2 , but how this nutrient is allocated among leaf functions remains poorly understood. Analyzing 520 plant species, this study finds a fundamental trade-off in leaf N partitioning between photosynthesis and cell walls, a pattern constrained by deep evolutionary history and modified by environmental factors.

item.title: Nature Communications: HDAC inhibition via suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid ameliorates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity
item.description: The study identifies a new mechanism of anthracycline cardiotoxicity in vivo and shows that the HDAC-inhibitor SAHA protects the heart by disrupting 14-3-3–HDAC4 signaling, thereby suppressing Topo IIb-linked MEF2-driven transcription.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cryo-EM structures of the SurA–BAM complex reveal conformational changes in outer membrane protein assembly
item.description: Outer membrane proteins are delivered to the BAM complex by the chaperone SurA for proper assembly. Here, the authors report multiple structures of the SurA–BAM complex and show that SurA undergoes conformational changes to pass substrates to BAM.

item.title: Nature Communications: Cadonilimab plus lenvatinib in advanced endometrial cancer: the multicenter single-arm phase II CLEAR-EC trial
item.description: Immune checkpoint blockade has emerged as a therapeutic option for patients with endometrial cancer. Here the authors report the results of a phase II trial of cadonilimab (a bispecific antibody targeting PD-1 and CTLA-4) combined with lenvatinib in advanced endometrial cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phylogenetic analysis of the 2025 Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
item.description: The study reports the emergence of a new Ebola variant in a remote area of Kasai Province, DR Congo. The findings highlight the need for rapid detection and sequencing to better identify variants and quickly respond to outbreaks.

item.title: Nature Communications: Effect of human urinary microenvironment and fluid flow on antibiotic and phage therapy efficacy against uropathogenic Escherichia coli
item.description: Maset et al. show that bladder conditions strongly influence how urinary tract infections respond to antibiotics and bacteriophages, highlighting the need for more realistic lab models to improve diagnosis and treatment of recurrent infections.

item.title: Nature Communications: Therapy induced senescence promotes immunogenicity in acute myeloid Leukemia through reduced EZH2 activity
item.description: Acute myeloid leukemia responses to chemotherapy vary, and the effects of therapy induced senescence on anti-tumor immunity remain unclear. Here, the authors show that chemotherapy-induced senescence increases antigen presentation and T-cell recognition of leukemia cells and enhances responses to immune checkpoint blockade, while EZH2 inhibition can restore these immune features in less responsive leukemias.

item.title: Nature Communications: The membrane-to-cortex distance regulates mDia1 activity to control cortical mechanics
item.description: The surface of mammalian cells is a multi-layered composite structure. The authors combine advanced biophysical methods with cryo-electron tomography to identify the gap between the membrane and the actin cortex as a critical geometrical parameter that controls cell surface mechanics.

item.title: Nature Communications: System-wide investments generate health and enhance HIV, TB and malaria control in Malawi
item.description: A modelling study of Malawi’s health system shows that combining health system strengthening with disease-targeted programmes delivers twice the return on investment and three times the health impact of disease-focused investment alone.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microenvironment-aware transcriptome reconstruction in spatial transcriptomics
item.description: Current methods for spatial transcriptomics data analysis do not fully capture context-dependent variation within cell types. Here the authors present Emerge, which integrates cellular identity with tissue environments to reveal hidden cellular states and microenvironment-associated transcriptional programs.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multiple overlapping SNARE complexes drive endosome maturation in Drosophila nephrocytes
item.description: Hargitai, Molnar et al. show that parallel, non-interchangeable SNARE complexes drive endosome maturation in Drosophila nephrocytes, revealing alternative routes that allow membrane progression toward lysosomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Perceived humanness and empathy are dissociated in relationship advice generated by a large language model
item.description: Large language models can generate empathic language similar to human writing. The authors show that empathic language and perceived humanness are dissociated, revealing stochastic empathy in AI systems.

item.title: Nature Communications: Weighted sliced inverse regression for scalable supervised dimensionality reduction of spatial transcriptomics data
item.description: Woollard and colleagues present wSIR, a dimension reduction method for spatial transcriptomics data. wSIR is scalable with its embedding constructed using spatial coordinates. Two case studies show how wSIR facilitates meaningful biological discovery.

item.title: Nature Communications: K-MARVEL: K-Mer-based antimicrobial resistance virtual exploration lab
item.description: Ahmad et al present K MARVEL, a scalable, flexible, memory-efficient solution for detection of antimicrobial resistance genes. K-MARVEL can handle data from both long- and short-read sequencing technologies, and resolve complex genomic scenarios, making it a potentially important tool for AMR surveillance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Distinct constraints but shared dynamics shape the macroevolution of volatile organic compound chemodiversity
item.description: Organisms produce volatile organic compounds for communication, defense and environmental responses, but how this chemodiversity evolved is unclear. This study shows that in gymnosperms, chemodiversity shows weak covariation, core compounds are highly integrated, and both evolve in a punctuated mode.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis for rosuvastatin-induced activation of skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor 1
item.description: Here the authors report the RyR1 calcium channel structure bound to rosuvastatin: rosuvastatin occupies the same binding site as simvastatin to activate the channel. This may provide a structural basis for developing statins with fewer muscle side effects.

item.title: Nature Communications: A spatial and temporal transcriptomic atlas of mouse intestinal regeneration in the jejunum
item.description: The intestinal epithelium efficiently regenerates after injury, yet the dynamics underlying this process are not fully understood. Here, the authors use spatial transcriptomics to map the mouse intestine over time after radiation injury, revealing shifts in villus zonation, spatially restricted interferon signaling, altered stem cell populations and a surge in gene transcription that may help fuel recovery.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-stage single-cell atlas of a chordate non-embryonic development unveils dedifferentiating bud founder cells
item.description: The cellular origins of non-embryonic body formation in chordates remain poorly understood. Here, using single-cell transcriptomics across seven stages of asexual development, the authors identify epithelial founder cells that acquire developmental potential through dedifferentiation, providing a cellular framework for non-embryonic body formation in a chordate.

item.title: Nature Communications: PIP2 binding at allosteric site blocks activation in human rod CNG channels
item.description: PIP2 is known to inhibit rod photoreceptor CNG channels, but the mechanism is unclear. Here, the authors combine functional assays and cryo-EM to show PIP2 binds an allosteric site in CNGA1, blocking conformational changes required for channel opening.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tuning of AMPA receptor activation by inhibitory auxiliary subunits and epilepsy-associated disease mutations
item.description: AMPA receptors mediate the majority of excitatory neurotransmission. Here, the authors report structural and functional regulation of GluA2 AMPA receptor by inhibitory auxiliary subunits GSG1L and TARP γ5 and by epilepsy-associated disease mutations.

item.title: Nature Communications: High-resolution structures of human NHE6 and NHE9 elucidate endosomal ion and lipid interactions
item.description: NHE6 and NHE9 regulate endosomal pH and are linked to neurological disease. Here, the authors report cryo-EM structures of human NHE9 and two NHE6 splice isoforms, revealing sodium and lipid- binding sites, including an NHE6 phosphoinositide pocket.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tumor-intrinsic IFNγ signaling and niche adaptation drive early colonization in ovarian cancer metastasis
item.description: The mechanisms enabling disseminating tumour cells (DTCs) to survive and colonise peritoneal niches in ovarian cancer metastasis remain poorly understood. Using single-cell barcoding, transcriptome profiling, and in vivo CRISPR screening, the authors identify a niche-adaptive IFNγ response signature that supports pioneer DTC outgrowth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Heterogeneity in the response to the metabolic environment drives fosfomycin heteroresistance
item.description: Choby et al . show an antibiotic-resistant subpopulation is generated by heterogeneity in expression of an antibiotic importer repressed by environmental glucose, suggesting diabetes-related infection environments may influence antibiotic resistance.

item.title: Nature Communications: Microbial-derived tryptophan metabolites in the infant gut associate with increased risk of asthma following cesarean section
item.description: Here, in the Canadian birth cohort (CHILD), the authors associate 1-year C-section-microbiome with higher asthma risk at age 5, as previously reported in the Danish birth cohort (COPSAC2010), and identify microbial-derived tryptophan metabolites at 1 year of age to mediate the association between C-section and asthma risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sensory plasticity of dorsal horn silent neurons as a critical mechanism for neuropathic pain
item.description: Nerve injury alters sensory processing leading to neuropathic pain. In this study, the authors show that loss of spinal inhibition after injury in mice does not seem to let nociceptive neurons be activated by innocuous stimuli, but rather unmasks a previously silent circuit which likely drives pain.

item.title: Nature Communications: Longitudinal evidence for decreasing statistical learning abilities across childhood
item.description: Through statistical learning, people extract patterns from the environment to predict future events. In a longitudinal study, the authors show that statistical learning declines with age and that higher executive functions are linked to this decline.

item.title: Nature Communications: Offline generative network reconfiguration guides insight-like accelerated learning by assimilation into schema in rats
item.description: Acquisition of a mental schema of associative abstract rules enables insight-like accelerated new related learning. The authors show that generative reconfiguration of hippocampus-prefrontal networks during sleep/rest in rats supports map-based accelerated learning and systems consolidation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diverse biosynthetic pathways in Arctic hydrothermal biofilms
item.description: Biosynthetic genes produced from microbes have unique industrial properties, however, the diversity of such genes from extreme environments remains limited. Here, the authors use meta-omics of Arctic hydrothermal vent biofilms and uncover nearly 3000 genes, including a possibility for hydrogen cyanide production in archaea.

item.title: Nature Communications: Increased encoding of aversive stimuli by lateral habenula neurons during Δ 9 -tetrahydrocannabinol withdrawal
item.description: Withdrawal from extended cannabis use is associated with negative emotional states. Here, the authors show that withdrawal from the psychoactive cannabis molecule, THC, increased lateral habenula excitability and the strength of fear conditioning.

item.title: Nature Communications: Spatial transcriptomics reveals laminar and cell-type-specific A-to-I RNA editing signatures in the macaque cortex
item.description: ADAR-mediated RNA editing is crucial for neuronal function, yet its spatial signatures in the cortex are unknown. Here, authors show that editing correlates with cortical hierarchy, and PV neurons exhibit the highest editing levels in most regions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Site-specific programming characterizes dynamic post-translational acetylation of histone H2B lysine 108 in mouse embryonic stem cells
item.description: The authors present a genetic code expansion-based platform in embryonic stem cells, revealing the functional significance of H2B-K108 acetylation during mESC differentiation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Motifs of brain cortical folding from birth to adulthood
item.description: Guo and colleagues parse cortical folding variability into a family of distinct anatomical motifs that generalise across adults and neonates. These motifs shed light on structural asymmetry, heritability, and folding-function links.

item.title: Nature Communications: Yellow protein co-opted to sustain obligate symbiosis in leaf beetles
item.description: Insects have evolved diverse strategies to protect their genome-reduced symbionts during vertical transmission. Here, authors show that tortoise beetles have co-opted a Yellow protein to form spheres that protect and transmit the symbiont Stammera .

item.title: Nature Communications: The urinary pathobiont Actinobaculum massiliense can generate androgens via the dirAB pathway
item.description: Urinary bacteria linked to prostate cancer are often overlooked. Here, the authors developed a high-throughput assay to identify androgen-producing urinary microbes, isolated key bacterial strains, and discovered genes and enzymes that enable steroid conversion, revealing mechanisms by which urinary bacteria may influence host hormone biology.

item.title: Nature Communications: Functional coupling between MC4R and Kir7.1 contributes to clozapine-induced weight gain in female mice
item.description: Antipsychotic drugs commonly cause overeating and weight gain, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, authors show that clozapine drives these effects in female mice by enhancing MC4R-Kir7.1 coupling in key appetite-regulating neurons.

item.title: Nature Communications: Redox-dependent synaptic clustering of gephyrin
item.description: Gehling et al show that cysteines in gephyrin regulate synaptic localization and clustering as redox-switches, thereby establishing a so far undefined link between neuronal and metabolic activity at inhibitory synapses.

item.title: Nature Communications: First-line tislelizumab plus chemotherapy versus placebo plus chemotherapy in unresectable advanced/metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: minimum 3-year survival follow-up of a randomized phase 3 trial (RATIONALE-306)
item.description: The RATIONALE-306 trial demonstrated improved overall survival in participants with advanced/metastatic esophageal squamous cell carcinoma treated with tislelizumab plus chemotherapy comparing with those who received placebo plus chemotherapy. Here they report its exploratory long-term efficacy/safety/quality of life analysis after 36.0 months follow-up.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extracellular vesicle proteins monitor and interfere with CLDN18.2-targeted CAR-T cell and antibody therapies against gastrointestinal cancers
item.description: CLDN18.2-targeted CART and antibody therapies are promising for gastrointestinal cancers, but predictive biomarkers and strategies to enhance efficacy are needed. Here, these authors investigate how extracellular vesicle (EV)- derived proteins influence therapeutic response to CLDN18.2-based CAR-T and targeted therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Functional annotation of insulin-responsive genes in human adipocytes reveals PLCXD1 as a lipid storage regulator
item.description: Frendo-Cumbo et al. combine transcriptomics with functional screening in adipocytes to identify PLCXD1 as an insulin-regulated gene. This atypical phospholipase is localized to early endosomes and promotes lipid storage in human fat cells.
